identity: An Arabic Wikipedia article on زجاج الخليل (Hebron glass): a long merged lead block covering the craft's Roman/Phoenician antiquity, the حارة القزازين quarter, annual output and export split, raw materials from recycled bottles, the trade's decline, pricing, the traditional melting process, and Israeli army damage; then a <NL>-delimited section heading التاريخ and three history paragraphs quoting the historians Bougie Poncet, Felix Fabri, Mariti (1767), Robinson (1834) and Bauerer (1843). Wikipedia-Arabic prose at its most run-on, with scan/typo scars: 'تجل' for تُجلب @245, 'إسرار' for أسرار @285, 'عل' for على @491, 'أنتقلت' for انتقلت @485.
law: §L as revised in batch 12 — Wikipedia article prose is FACT-LISTING and each و + finite verb is normally a new fact and a new segment (~5:1). Measured result here: 44 boundaries over 669 tokens = 15.2 tokens/segment. This is NOT the 25-45 band of the §L/LAW 6 table (that band belongs to translated monographs, §Z) and it is not §Y's 11 either. The cut inventory is lexical and dense: asyndetic fresh finite clauses (تشكل، تعتمد، يستعمل، تتنوع، مثال آخر), و + verb (وتلاقي، ولا تزال، ويقدر، وتتوزع، وتم، ويعتقد، وساعد، ووصف، وأشار، وذكر), discourse openers (لذا، لقد، أما…ف، فمنذ، فقد، بينما، إلا أن، ولكن، لكن), and every fronted adverbial (ومن أهم، في الوقت الحاضر، حسب الحفريات، من أهم الصادرات) with the boundary placed BEFORE it.
reasoning:
Welds I had to defend, all from the protected list:
- @12، @28، @129، @295 — والتي / الذين / والذين relative pronouns. Never a boundary, however long the chain. The lead sentence runs 35 tokens on two والتي clauses and stays whole.
- @189 عمليا before وذلك بسبب — the trailing وذلك adjunct that cost me a false cut in doc_2fabc1ccf342 (LAW 4, Q1). Weld.
- @159 الصهر before وتوفر الروح الإبداعية — و + verbal noun coordinated with تحمل, both predicates of ومن أهم متطلبات. LAW 0''' item 1.
- @76-96, the export split '50 إلى إسرائيل 40 إلى أوروبا … و 10 تسوق إلى الدول العربية' — a comma-list after على النحو. LAW 3 as revised: lists are ONE segment, 27 tokens of it. There is no <NL> anywhere in the run, so it was inline prose, not a bulleted list.
- @317 المصنوعة before وتشمل — 'تتنوع المنتوجات المصنوعة وتشمل…' is two verbs on one subject with no new participant, the tight-pair case (LAW 0''' item 2), and the segment is only 15 tokens.
- @1 الخليل — I do NOT cut after the article lemma. 'زجاج الخليل صناعة الزجاج والخزف…' is a well-formed Arabic nominal sentence needing no copula, and headings in this document carry <NL> on both sides (see التاريخ @331) while this does not.
Contested cuts:
@197 فلسطين before حيث يتوجه البعض. B2 offers both readings — حيث could hang off 'في فلسطين' as a locative adjunct and weld. I cut, on the batch-14 Z3 finding that this family of connectives is REGISTER-CONDITIONED: they weld in long-unit scholarly prose (where كما welded in doc_c0adf987ac2e) and cut in short-unit registers, which is what doc_7b090cf754e8 ('مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي ‖ حيث يقومون') and doc_a4029b2c8e1b ('القوى العظمى ‖ حيث ورد') already showed. At 15 tokens/segment this document is squarely short-unit. Medium.
@345 أراضيها before وتطورت بشكل واضح — و + finite verb with the same subject but genuinely new material (a new time frame, 'after the coming of Islam'). Batch 12's Borussia Dortmund lesson was that all five misses were exactly this shape. Medium.
@566 and @575, inside the Mariti report. G1 says a quotation never separates from its speech verb, and I keep that at the front edge — 'فقد ذكر المؤرخ ماريتي عام 1767 يتم تصنيع الأساور…' is one segment. But I do NOT extend G1 across the whole 35-token report: this is not a conversational turn, it is encyclopedic paraphrase, and its two ويصدر / ويتم clauses are fresh facts of the same kind that cut everywhere else in the article. Same treatment for the Robinson report at @596/@606 and the Bauerer report at @636. Medium — the alternative reading (whole report = one segment) would give three segments of 35, 19 and 36 tokens in a 15-token register.
Density by block: lead 17.4, history-1 15.0, history-2 15.1, history-3 12.3. The lead runs highest because its long segments are genuinely relative-clause chains with no available joint.
